gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-graduate: Bookish and dignified, Graduate sets a stately tone underneath. Comic Relief does its best work shouting, with uniform strokes and half-open bowls, while Graduate, a text serif, is made for quiet reading.
gen-gf-cousine-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Typewriter stiffness up top, then a smooth bent-steel line underneath. Cousine excels at precise, isolated letters, while Be Vietnam Pro is best at carrying a constant stroke through whole lines.
gen-gf-cousine-fs-ranade: Precise and typewriter-stiff, Cousine keeps every glyph in its own space. That rigid clarity is its best trick, while Ranade, a sans-serif, does better with softly shifting weight and widely spaced stroke ends.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-montserrat: Relaxed and inviting, Delius Unicase writes like a friendly hand. Its best move is loose, untapered handwriting, whereas Montserrat, a sans, is best at gliding geometric curves with oversized counters.
gen-gf-edu-vic-wa-nt-hand-fs-literata: Hand-drawn warmth fills Edu VIC WA NT Hand, tall capitals over small lowercase. That looseness earns its keep big and short, while Literata, a serif with sturdy thin strokes and slightly heavier thick ones, takes over.
gen-gf-esteban-general-sans: Refined and bookish up top, Esteban has tall middle letters and moderate contrast. And General Sans, a sans-serif with steady pressure and a smooth path around each bend, keeps text flowing easily.
gen-gf-fira-code-fs-supreme: Typewriter rhythm, wide berth around every letter: Fira Code feels like a tidy grid of generous lowercase. Supreme, a sans-serif, then reads crisp and sturdy, its letters held open.
gen-gf-fira-code-gf-cascadia-mono: Wide-berth typewriter letters up top, then a tight, pin-straight line below. What stands out most is the tall lowercase of Fira Code against the compact, level skyline of Cascadia Mono.
gen-gf-fira-mono-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code draws a wire-like monoline skeleton with room around every neighbor, a modern counterweight to the blocky words of Fira Mono. Generous spacing runs through both, and that is the draw.
gen-gf-fira-mono-montserrat: Fira Mono lines its letters up in solid blocks with see-through openings, giving words a steady, monospaced beat. Montserrat then glides in beneath, its round letters drawn like bent wire.
